name: Tang blue-painted white stoneware
summary: Tang-era potters at Gongxian in Henan painted white-slipped stoneware with cobalt blue; three such dishes sank around 850 CE in the Belitung shipwreck's export cargo.
description: Gongxian high-fired white-slip stoneware vessels decorated with cobalt blue; technically distinct from later Jingdezhen blue-and-white.
tier_reason: A particular early blue-painted ceramic branch fits2; do not equate it with the later Yuan technology. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: A decorative product type from one kiln complex, made in small numbers with no established descent to later blue-and-white; scores imply tier 3, below the reviewed tier 2.

why: Cobalt-blue designs suited buyers in West Asia, the likely market for much of the Belitung ship's cargo.

places.note: Belitung shipwreck, found off Belitung Island

date.label: by c. 850 CE
date.basis: The Belitung ship sailed around the second quarter of the ninth century with three complete blue-and-white dishes; its departure date is approximate.

events.statement: Three Gongxian blue-and-white dishes were included in the ship’s merchant cargo.
events.place_note: Belitung shipwreck, found off Belitung Island
events.population: Maritime traders carrying the Belitung ship’s Gongxian wares
events.caveats: The precise kiln and decoration sequence remain scholarly interpretations; shipment does not establish an eventual sale or receiver.

evidence.supports: Identifies the wreck dishes, their approximate ninth-century context, production method, export orientation and separately developed later blue-and-white tradition.
